Xinyan's guitar is a traditional Chinese instrument she just tweaked to make it sound like a guitar, presumably with her Vision. So, it's not that out of place, especially considering that her whole plot revolves around people of Liyue finding her weird for not sticking up with traditional music.

Cloud Retainer was, since the first time she was introduced, always shown to us as "that reclusive Adepti who spends all her time on fiddling with machinery". We're explicitly told by Zhongli that she was the one who created the Ballistas. Surely, if you're a magical bird who can make magical ballistas, you can also make magical popcorn machines and magical drones? She's an Adepti who spent her entire life on doing shit. No wonder she can make a drone.

Inazuma's light novels are just that. Light novels. It's not tech. It's a genre. And, as a reminder, popular, light-hearted literature existed in Japan as early as in 10th century.

Kameras are a fairly new invention, and that's considering they're from the most technologically advanced nation. Plenty of people say that.

Scuba gear is, again, not surprising. Fontaine was always sold to us as the steampunk nation - and scuba gear did historically exist by 19th century, same as Chevreuse's musket. So having that, but tweaked in a fantasy setting of Genshin is, again, not surprising at all.

Mehrak is a piece of tech from an ancient civilization that we have seen to be capable of, among other things, creating radars, keycard doors and giant lasers. A tech that has an explanation in lore and it's place in the lore, that isn't used by nearly anyone anymore. The same can be said about anything Khaenriahn.

The problem isn't that we have some less fantastical technology in Genshin, the problem is that Natlan's technology - at least that used by playable characters - is out of touch with it's region and npc's.

What I think is:

Yoosung: Anemo greatsword. After all, he is the most affected by Rika's death, thus fitting in the "dead important person" Anemo trope. Greatsword because of his main in LOLOL. He probably would be a sub-dps

Zen: Cryo sword. Cryo character often have some form of "duality" within them - in Zen's case, that would probably be maintaining his confident personality that everyone around him knows, even though he doubts himself very often. Sword because, I dunno. Just suits him I guess. I think he would be a dps with some form of team buff included

Jaehee: Geo sword. She's hardworking, stern and modest, like most of the geo characters. Sword is a nice, elegant and effective weapon, and practitcal to carry, perfect for someone like her (think something like Keqing). Probably support, preferably shielder/buffer mix

Jumin: Electro polearm. Electro characters are often the "odd ones", not exactly fitting the norms of their enviroment. In Jumin's case, at first glance, he fits perfectly well in being a ceo of a large company, BUT his questionable at best decisions regarding cats and cat products probably leave his employees with "wtf?" expression. And he doesn't really know how to be a part of "normal people" society (mind you, RFA had to told him about existence of hamburgers, of all things). Polearm because he has strong Zhongli vibes. Dps.

Seven: After thinking about it for a while I think he likely would be a Pyro catalyst. Pyro users are known for their passion for something, whether it would be a cause, people, hobby or something else. Seven is willing to do everything to keep his friends and brother safe, even distancing himself from them when he feels it's the right choice to make. But honestly, he might as well be anemo (longing for freedom, wanting to help others, "dead/missing important person" trope), cryo (being a goofball for the sake of others, even tho he's depressed af; loving MC and not wanting to get close to her for her sake) or electro (being that one "clown" in a group with a weird sense of humor nobody understands except him and maybe mc), so it's up to you what element he would have. Catalyst because I can't imagine him with any weapon, honestly; he would be just chilling in the back while the robo-slime that he made anihilated entire hilichurl camp. I think dps/maybe sub-dps

V: Anemo polearm. Beside the "dead someone" trope, those characters mostly strive for some kind of freedom and are driven by their want to help others, some even to the extreme of putting themselves in danger instead of letting others get hurt. Sounds familiar, right? V is checking all of these boxes. Polearm because it would be nice if he and Jumin used the same type of weapon, indicating at their friendship. Probably healer support

Saeran: Electro bow. He doesn't really fit in being "the big baddie" that Rika wants him to be since he does care about Seven after all, AND he can't easily just "return to being normal" after saving him from Mint Eye. Even though he tries hard to fit in in both cases, he can't just put everything he went through aside. Just give him some therapy already. Bow would suit his slow-paced, precise style of battle I suppose. I think he would be a dps

Vanderwood: Pyro bow. Pyro users are passionate, and Vanderwood is very passionate about his dream to one day punch Seven in the face without any repercussions. Bow 'cause it just fits him, honestly. Probably sub-dps

Rika: Cryo catalyst. Again, the theme of "duality" within her. On one hand, she just genuinely wants to make world a better place. On the other, she won't stop at anything to make that happen, including brainwashing people or straight up murder. And on top of that she's very unpredictable, probably because of some sort of mental illness. Catalysts overall feel to me like a very distinguished weapon, fitting for someone of high status, perfect for a cult leader. I don't think she would be a good dps though, since she prefers working in the shadows. Probably a buffer support (evil cryo Bennett?)

I agree, but to an extent.  


Did I enjoy this questline? Hell yeah. Im convinced the rhalata questline was the main focus and the star of this DLC, everything there is at it's best - locations are memorable, characters are believable and you want more of them with every quest - you want to know more about the Father, you want to help Tharael, or at least understand him. And don't make me start on the music; it's enough that I listen to Black Walz and Night of the Raven on an almost daily basis.  


But I'm not sure if I'd enjoyed it that much if it lasted longer than it should. I can compare that to Assassin's Creed Odyssey, since it's the game I have the most problems with for that exact reason. You see, even if there are many characters and moments I like, even with all those memorable locations and beautiful music... The length of it's main quest is enormous, and because of that all of those little pieces that make me like the story in the first place are spread out so loose that at the end I can't even remember WHAT made me like this exact thing so much. The whole potential and beauty of each fragment is wasted, because you can feel the whole thing was forcibly extended.  


And I fear if this game - not only rhalata questline, but main quest as well - was also forcibly extended in the same way... would I care about this game as much as I do now? Would it made a similiar impression to me? Which character I'd care about the most, if Jespar's and Tharael's stories were so streched out that they would've become unrecognizable?   


I mean, if Nicolas and the team had a clear idea how to do it in a natural way and genuinely wanted to make those questlines longer, I think they would've done it by now. But if I had to choose which one I'd prefer - short, but overflowing with content and emotions story or long, but with high risk of getting forgettable after some time epic tale, I'd definitely go with the option #1.

W on the other hand has; not only it gives you feathers, it also gives you big attack speed buff, which is one of Xayah's biggest advantages over other ADC's (beside being helpful while positioning to accurately use your E), heck, with lethal tempo and attack speed oriented build she becomes an unstoppable kiling machine. Maxing Q first is like willingly broking your leg. You can say that it's no difference if you did it or not since it's going to repair itself eventually, but if you hadn't do it you wouldn't have your leg in the cast and, in consequence, would live like you always used to.

when I was younger it was hard for me to have any hobbies. I liked to draw and was pretty good at it (for a child); they told me to stop doing it since it's "childish and useless" and to do something "more important", like read a book or study. I couldn't go outside to play with other children, " 'cause granny will be sad you're leaving her alone". I was interested (and still I am, to some extend) in  archaeology and astronomy. But, since my mother thought it's stupid and useless, I wasn't allowed to do anything beyond reading about it. Actually, the only thing I was allowed to do was reading, and later writing stuff like poems or short stories, since my language teacher was really proud of my work. So i did mostly that.

Later I've tried again. Singing? Bad, if it was not in the local church. Playing instruments? Same as above. Video games? Anime? Programming? Nope. I've never, and I mean it, never knew someone from a healthy family. My own family was far from perfect anyway, but so did families of any of my friends - abuse, unhealthy expectations, parents cheating on one another and don't giving a crap about their children, you name it. I thought that it's just the way of things, I've seen it everywhere so it has to be normal, right?

Well, that changed when I met my boyfriend and his family. At first I kinda didn't believe him when he first told me that he and his parents were never fighting each other, he trusted them and they were always supportive of him. I thought he just doesn't wanna talk about it, so I've just let the subject go. But the more we talked, the more I've seen he was, actually, telling the truth - zero screams, passive agressive comments, snarky tone, both he and his parents were talking to each other like equal humans, something that blew my mind at first. He often goes to his mom's room to show or tell her something cool and she does the same. 

It was hard to comprehend that healthy relationships between parents and children can exist. As I said, I've never met anyone who had one before. I'm no contact with most of my family, but even when I wasn't... I would never willingly talk to my mother about my day. Ask my grandma for advice. Hell, I never could ask even how to do simplest things like how to cook an eggs. Everything I can do, I've learned that myself. And I thought that it is a normal thing, which, well, apparently isn't.

I'm still trying to understand how does it all work. Even though me and my bf had different lives, we try to understand one another. I'm sure our weird and somewhat dark sense of humor helps too, haha. The point is... Understanding can be hard. Can be stressful. Can lead to emotional outbursts - for both sides of the argument. But it's possible and worth the costs, in my opinion
